newsitem.title: UK: U.S stocks in London steady, await economic data.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks in London steady, await economic data.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady to slightly firmer on Monday but many European investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of a plethora of U.S. economic statistics due later this week.

Gross domestic product and consumer confidence are among the figures scheduled for release but the market is expected to once again hold its final judgement until Friday's publication of unemployment and wage cost numbers, dealers said.
"The Dow will churn this week and may lose a bit of ground but I don't look for any huge movement until we see the jobs data," one dealer said.
Tobacco stocks were a bit higher after sliding in New York on Friday amid fears that the industry may have to cough up more money if there is a negotiated settlement of U.S. lawsuits.
The industry was dealt a blow on Friday when a U.S. judge ruled that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration could regulate sales and labelling of cigarettes.

The decision by U.S. District Court Judge William Osteen was the first time a court had ruled that nicotine is a drug and will strengthen the hand of anti-smoking forces in ongoing litigation talks, analysts said.
"We've seen a bit of bottom fishing in the tobaccos but no real volumes," one market maker said.
Philip Morris Cos Inc, which fell $2-1/4 on Friday, was up $1/8 to $39-1/2 while RJR Nabisco Holdings rose $1/4 to $29-1/4 after slipping $2-5/8.
IBM was up $1/8 to $150-7/8 ahead of its annual shareholders meeting on Tuesday. "People are hoping IBM will announce a more aggressive share buyback plan," one dealer said.

In the first quarter, IBM spent about $2 billion buying back its own stock, under its current authorisation plan, reducing the number of its shares outstanding to 501.7 million, from 544.3 million a year ago.
Elsewhere, Boeing Co was down $3/8 to $101-5/8 after a report in the London Times newspaper said Airbus Industries was in merger talks with Lockheed Martin.
"A merger seems unlikely but some people fear the two might set up joint ventures which would put pressure on Boeing," a market maker said.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.25 to 768.70 by 1140 GMT while the June T-bond rose 1/32 to 107-6/32. The yield on the 30-year cash long bond was standing at 7.14 percent.
